tracks.title: Why Smart Bathrooms Fail (PIR & mmWave Trap)
tracks.script_text: Most smart bathrooms fail for one simple reason: sensors hate steam. PIR motion sensors can't see through glass shower cabins, mmWave radars suffer from reflection noise, and battery-powered sensors die in high humidity. Even worse, naive rules like "turn light on when door closes" leave you stepping into pitch darkness.

tracks.title: Physical Boundary Determinism (MC-38 Reed Switch)
tracks.script_text: The Apartment Thread bathroom pattern solves this with physical boundary determinism. Because every bathroom has a door, we use a simple, passive MC-38 magnetic reed switch. Sourced for under sixty rupees, the magnet mounts on the moving door leaf, while the sensor body mounts on the exterior door jamb, completely isolated from hot shower steam and condensation.

tracks.title: In-Wall Dummy Channel Wiring (Tinxy S2 Decoupling)
tracks.script_text: In Indian apartments, the switchboard is directly adjacent to the door frame. Instead of adding a wireless transmitter with batteries, we pull a thin, mains-insulated two-core wire straight into the switchboard. Connected to switch input S2 of an in-wall Tinxy module as a dummy channel, the dry contact triggers the onboard microcontroller directly.

tracks.title: The 4-State Presence Engine (Sub-5ms Local Logic)
tracks.script_text: A sub-five-millisecond state machine runs directly on chip silicon. When the door opens from outside with the light off, the light turns on instantly before you step inside, starting a sixty-second entry timer. When you pull the door shut, occupancy latches: lights and exhaust fan stay locked on continuously, even if you are standing completely still in the shower. When you finish and open the door, a sixty-second exit timer begins, turning everything off once vacant.

tracks.title: 100% Local-First & Fail-Safe Architecture
tracks.script_text: Because this logic runs locally on the switchboard's microcontroller, it works with zero cloud and zero hub dependency. Even if Wi-Fi, Thread, or Home Assistant goes offline, the bathroom automates seamlessly. And the physical wall switches retain complete mechanical override at all times. Reliable, shower-proof, and battery-free.
